hi.cs_note: The examples below are representative delivery patterns based on real service-business scenarios. They are written to show scope logic, not to pretend we have public permission to disclose every client detail.
hi.cs_manifesto_title: The studio does not start from aesthetics. It starts from the commercial decision the site has to support.
hi.cs_manifesto_text: Every pattern below comes from the same operating logic: trust first, scope before build and public execution only when the surface is strong enough to be checked by real buyers.
hi.cs_manifesto_li1: We review the live site, not a pitch deck.
hi.cs_manifesto_li2: We isolate where trust, positioning or qualification are breaking.
hi.cs_manifesto_li3: We answer with a written path that can be built, reviewed and checked.
hi.cs_case1_title: Weak trust layer on a service-business homepage
hi.cs_case1_meta: Typical issue: the website explains the business, but does not make the next step feel safe or commercially clear.
hi.cs_case1_li1: Homepage promise rewritten around the actual decision the client has to make.
hi.cs_case1_li2: Contact path simplified so the visitor is not pushed through unnecessary friction.
hi.cs_case1_li3: Trust assets reorganized: proof, FAQs, operational detail and reassurance.
hi.cs_case2_title: Luxury or hospitality offer with weak value perception
hi.cs_case2_meta: Typical issue: the service may be expensive and real, but the site still looks generic or operationally thin.
hi.cs_case2_li1: Offer tiers restructured so premium value is visible before pricing is discussed.
hi.cs_case2_li2: Visual hierarchy rebuilt to support authority, exclusivity and booking confidence.
hi.cs_case2_li3: Packages, extras and enquiry path aligned to higher-quality quotes.
hi.cs_case3_title: Professional service site generating the wrong type of inquiry
hi.cs_case3_meta: Typical issue: the business sounds competent, but the website qualifies almost nobody and leaves the offer too abstract.
hi.cs_case3_li1: Service pages reframed around sector, problem and commercial relevance.
hi.cs_case3_li2: Quote forms reduced to the fields that matter for qualification.
hi.cs_case3_li3: Written scope model used to separate serious leads from generic requests.
hi.cs_protocol_title: Every case begins with the same discipline: verify the live site, frame the scope, build with control points.
hi.cs_protocol_lead: The work starts from the existing site, not from a moodboard. The commercial problem is identified first, then structure, implementation and launch steps are documented.
hi.cs_protocol_card1_d: Homepage, contact path, offer clarity and visible trust gaps are reviewed before any proposal is written.
hi.cs_protocol_card2_d: The proposal explains what changes, why it changes and what commercial outcome the intervention is meant to improve.
hi.cs_protocol_card3_d: Build, revision and rollout are handled through explicit milestones so the client is not left inside a black box.
hi.cs_protocol_card4_d: No page is rebuilt on assumptions alone. Scope, priorities and commercial terms are confirmed in writing first.
